Let

\[
P=4\Theta(1-\Theta).
\]

Given \(P\), the two samples are independent iid Bernoulli\((P)\), so all information shared by \((X_1,\dots,X_n)\) and \((Y_1,\dots,Y_n)\) is carried by their numbers of ones

\[
K=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i,\qquad L=\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i.
\]

Thus

\[
I((X_1,\ldots,X_n);(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n))=I(K;L).
\]

Now compute the law of \(P\). For \(p=4\theta(1-\theta)\), the two preimages are

\[
\theta=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1-p}}2,
\]

and

\[
\left|\frac{d\theta}{dp}\right|=\frac1{4\sqrt{1-p}}.
\]

Since the Beta\((a,a)\) density is symmetric,

\[
f_P(p)
=2\cdot \frac{(p/4)^{a-1}}{B(a,a)}\cdot \frac1{4\sqrt{1-p}}
=\frac{p^{a-1}(1-p)^{-1/2}}{B(a,1/2)}.
\]

So

\[
P\sim \operatorname{Beta}\left(a,\frac12\right).
\]

For a one-dimensional Bernoulli parameter with prior density \(f\), the asymptotic mutual information between two independent samples of size \(n\) with common parameter is

\[
I(K;L)
=
\frac12\log n
+h(P)
+\frac12\mathbb E\log\frac1{P(1-P)}
-\frac12\log(4\pi e)
+o(1).
\]

Here the endpoint singularity at \(P=1\) is integrable; the region \(1-P\lesssim n^{-1}\) has prior mass \(O(n^{-1/2})\), so it contributes \(o(1)\).

For \(P\sim\operatorname{Beta}(\alpha,\beta)\),

\[
h(P)=\log B(\alpha,\beta)
-(\alpha-1)\psi(\alpha)
-(\beta-1)\psi(\beta)
+(\alpha+\beta-2)\psi(\alpha+\beta),
\]

and

\[
\mathbb E\log P=\psi(\alpha)-\psi(\alpha+\beta),\qquad
\mathbb E\log(1-P)=\psi(\beta)-\psi(\alpha+\beta).
\]

Taking \(\alpha=a,\ \beta=\tfrac12\),

\[
h(P)+\frac12\mathbb E\log\frac1{P(1-P)}
=
\log B\left(a,\frac12\right)
+\left(a-\frac12\right)
\left[
\psi\left(a+\frac12\right)-\psi(a)
\right].
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\log B\left(a,\frac12\right)
+\left(a-\frac12\right)\left(\psi\left(a+\frac12\right)-\psi(a)\right)
-\frac12\log(4\pi e)
}
\]
